independentScientificRequirements: Average power is energy per full period divided by that period; repeated steady periodic cycles permit a many-cycle average.
For a fixed ideal pure resistance R, instantaneous dissipation is p=i^2R and mean dissipation depends on the mean of i^2, not the square of the signed mean of i.
The sine/cosine peak divided by sqrt(2) relation is restricted to sinusoidal waveforms; the root-of-mean-square definition is more general.
The printed bar placement in the current formulas must remain literal. Faithful preservation does not make its conventional mathematical interpretation correct.

With i=I_m cos(omega t), cos(2 omega t) has period T/2; samples separated by T/4 are opposite. A quarter-period interval beginning at t=0 is not all positive. Sign-uniform T/4 intervals require an appropriate starting phase.
Equal DC and AC Joule energy in the same resistance uses the same duration and an averaging duration covering full cycles, or the long-time periodic regime. It is not an arbitrary subcycle equality.
P=I^2R=UI uses RMS U and I for the same purely resistive segment. It is not the general real-power law for phase-shifted reactive AC circuits.
The conventional AC-meter claim is read within the source's sinusoidal setting; arbitrary waveform accuracy or universal true-RMS instrumentation must not be invented.

baselineConcerns.reason: For the explicitly specified nonzero cosine current, its signed cycle mean is zero while its mean square is positive. The printed current bar covers i, unlike the voltage bar covering u^2. Prose describing RMS cannot itself validate the displayed square-of-mean identities. No correction or new erratum is authorized.

The zero mean is valid, but the source's each-quarter positive/next-quarter negative wording lacks the phase boundary required by cos(2 omega t). Test the candidate's text independently; do not use unopened figure 36 as evidence.
